seoDescription: Learn how to paint a room like a professional with expert tips from Monica from The Weekender. This comprehensive guide walks you through every step, from selecting the perfect paint color and sheen to calculating the right amount of paint for your space. Discover the best techniques for cutting in around ceilings, windows, and baseboards, and master different wall rolling methods for a flawless, smooth finish. Finish the job with crisp, clean trim for a result you'll love. Perfect for beginners and DIYers alike.

chapters.title: Introduction & Prep Review
chapters.description: An overview of the painting process and a reminder that proper room preparation is a critical first step.

chapters.title: How to Choose a Paint Color and Sheen
chapters.description: Learn how to select the right color using swatches in your room's lighting and choose the appropriate sheen for walls and trim.

chapters.title: Calculating How Much Paint to Buy
chapters.description: A professional painter helps calculate the required amount of paint for walls and trim, with a tip for using an online calculator.

chapters.title: Paint Prep: Opening, Stirring & Project Order
chapters.description: Covers how to open and stir paint, the debate on painting walls vs. trim first, when to use a primer, and how to 'box' paint.

chapters.title: The Art of Cutting In
chapters.description: This chapter covers brush selection, proper loading and holding techniques, and how to paint corners and edges before rolling.

chapters.title: Pro Tip: Cutting in the Ceiling Line
chapters.description: Watch a professional demonstrate how to achieve a perfectly straight paint line along the ceiling without using tape.

chapters.title: Choosing and Preparing Your Roller
chapters.description: Understand the different types of roller naps and sizes, and learn how to properly prepare your paint tray and load your roller.

chapters.title: Wall Rolling Techniques and Error Correction
chapters.description: Explore three common wall rolling methods and learn how to fix mistakes like roller lines and 'holidays' while the paint is still wet.

chapters.title: Preparing to Paint Trim
chapters.description: After the walls are dry, learn how to remove tape and properly tape off floors and walls to ensure a clean trim painting job.

chapters.title: Painting the Trim for a Professional Finish
chapters.description: See the final trim painting process using a clean angled brush and semi-gloss paint for a sharp, durable result.

chapters.title: Storing Paint and Final Thoughts
chapters.description: Properly seal and label your leftover paint for future touch-ups and review the key steps to a successful paint job.

summary:
## Key Concepts for Painting a Room

### Choosing Your Paint
- **Color**: Take paint swatches home and tape them to the wall. Observe them for a few days in different lighting conditions (day and night) to see how the color truly looks in your space.
- **Sheen**: Different sheens have different properties and looks.
  - **Flat/Matte**: Ideal for walls, especially for beginners, as it hides imperfections well.
  - **Semi-Gloss**: The standard for trim, doors, and window casings. It's durable, washable, and its reflective quality makes the trim stand out.

### Calculating Quantity
- **Walls**: One gallon of paint typically covers **400 square feet**. To calculate your needs, measure your walls and subtract the area of large windows and doors.
- **Trim**: One gallon of trim paint can cover **300-400 linear feet**.

> [!TIP]
> If math isn't your strong suit, use the online **Lowe's Paint Calculator** to easily determine how much paint you need.

### Paint Preparation
- **Stir, Don't Shake**: After opening your paint can (a 5-in-1 tool works great), use a stir stick to thoroughly mix the base and tint, which can separate over time. Scrape the bottom of the can as you stir.
- **Boxing Paint**: For large projects requiring multiple gallons, mix them all together in a larger (e.g., 5-gallon) bucket. This process, called **boxing**, ensures perfect color consistency across the entire room.

### The Painting Process: Walls First
1.  **Primer**: A **paint-and-primer-in-one** is sufficient for most jobs. Use a separate primer only for new, unpainted drywall or to cover significant stains.
2.  **Order of Operations**: It's recommended for beginners to paint **walls first**, then **trim**. This allows you to tape off the trim for protection from roller splatter. A clean trim job is the final touch that makes the whole room look professional.
3.  **Cutting In**: Use a 2-inch angled brush to paint the edges first—corners, along the ceiling, and around trim and windows. Paint a 3-inch band so your roller can overlap it slightly without hitting the adjacent surface.
4.  **Rolling**: After cutting in, use a roller for the main wall surfaces.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Always fix drips, globs, or roller lines while the paint is **still wet**. It's much easier to smooth them out with a brush or a drier roller than it is to sand and fix them once they've dried.

### Technique: Rolling the Walls
- **Roller Nap**: The thickness of the roller cover is called the **nap**. Use a **3/8" nap** for smooth interior walls. Use a thicker nap (e.g., 3/4") for rougher surfaces like stucco or masonry.
- **Loading the Roller**: Roll the cover into the paint in the tray's well, then roll it back and forth on the textured ramp to evenly distribute the paint without overloading it. 
- **Rolling Methods**: All methods work if they result in an even finish. Common techniques include:
    - The **"W" or "V" method** to distribute paint across a section, then filling it in.
    - **Top-to-bottom long strokes** for consistent coverage.

### Finishing with Trim
- After the walls are fully dry, tape off the floor and (optionally) the wall to protect them.
- Use a clean, angled brush and **semi-gloss paint** for the trim. Apply with smooth, even strokes for a crisp, clean line.

### Storing Leftover Paint
- Clean the rim of the paint can.
- Place the lid on top and gently tap it shut with a **rubber mallet** to create a good seal without damaging the can.
- Use a permanent marker to **label the lid** with the room and surface (e.g., "Bedroom #2 - Walls"). This makes future touch-ups effortless.
